slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A linear pair is two adjacent angles whose outer sides are opposite rays. By the Protractor Postulate, the angles in a linear pair are supplementary.

When two lines cross they form two pairs of vertical angles, angles whose sides are opposite rays.

Theorem: vertical angles are equal.

Proof: angles 1 and 2 form a linear pair, and so do angles 2 and 3. So both angle 1 and angle 3 are supplements of angle 2, and supplements of the same angle are equal.

slides.title: Try it
slides.html:
Rotate two crossing lines and watch the four angle measures.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Two lines cross and one angle is 47 degrees. Find the other three.
slides.reveal: Its vertical angle is 47; the other two are 180 − 47 = 133 degrees each.
